Sentence Structure.title: ordre des mots de base
points: ordre des mots de base pour les déclarations
sourcePoints: basic word order in simple statements
subject usually comes before the verb
if the verb takes an object, put it after the verb

Sentence Structure.title: parties de la phrase
points: emplacement de l'objet et du complément
sourcePoints: a complete clause needs a subject
a complete clause needs a main verb
an object or complement can follow the verb

Sentence Structure.title: ajouter des détails
points: temps à la fin de la phrase
sourcePoints: add a time phrase after the main clause (for example, at noon or yesterday)
add a place phrase after the time phrase (for example, at the station or in the kitchen)
Sentence Structure.example: Elle l'a rencontré à midi à la gare.
Sentence Structure.sourceExample: She met him at noon at the station.

mistakes.wrong: Elle l'a rencontré à la station de midi.
mistakes.fix: Elle l'a rencontré à midi à la gare.
mistakes.sourceWrong: She met him at noon the station.
mistakes.sourceFix: She met him at noon at the station.

Sentence Structure.title: lier des propositions
points: ajout de la clause de raison
ajout de la clause de temps
sourcePoints: main clause gives the core message
use a connector to link clauses (for example, because or when)
the linked clause needs its own subject and verb
Sentence Structure.example: Je suis resté à la maison parce qu'il a plu.
Sentence Structure.sourceExample: I stayed home because it rained.

mistakes.wrong: Je suis resté à la maison parce que.
mistakes.fix: Je suis resté à la maison parce qu'il a plu.
mistakes.sourceFix: I stayed home because it rained.

Sentence Structure.title: variété des phrases
sourcePoints: use short sentences for key points
use longer sentences for supporting detail
separate independent clauses with correct punctuation
Sentence Structure.example: Nous avons fini tôt. Nous sommes rentrés chez nous après le cours parce que nous étions fatigués.
Sentence Structure.sourceExample: We finished early. We went home after class because we were tired.

Verbs.title: verbes d'action
points: les verbes d'action montrent ce que fait le sujet
dans une phrase simple, placez le verbe d'action apr?s le sujet
s'il y a un objet, placez-le apr?s le verbe d'action
sourcePoints: action verbs show what the subject does
in simple statements, place the action verb after the subject
if there is an object, place it after the action verb

Verbs.title: verbes d'état
points: les verbes d'?tat d?crivent une condition, une pens?e, un sentiment ou une possession
dans une phrase simple, placez le verbe d'?tat apr?s le sujet
les verbes d'?tat ne sont g?n?ralement pas utilis?s aux formes continues
sourcePoints: state verbs describe a condition, thought, feeling, or possession
in simple statements, place the state verb after the subject
state verbs are usually not used in continuous forms

Verbs.title: verbes de liaison
points: les verbes de liaison relient le sujet ? un compl?ment
dans une phrase simple, placez le verbe de liaison apr?s le sujet
utilisez un adjectif ou un nom comme compl?ment apr?s le verbe de liaison
sourcePoints: linking verbs connect the subject to a complement
place the linking verb after the subject in a simple statement
use an adjective or noun as the complement after the linking verb

Verbs.title: schémas verbaux
points: certains verbes prennent un objet direct (verbe + objet)
certains verbes prennent un compl?ment adjectival (verbe + adjectif)
certains verbes prennent un groupe pr?positionnel (verbe + pr?position + groupe nominal)
sourcePoints: some verbs are followed by a preposition phrase
after the verb and object, add the required preposition
complete the preposition with a noun phrase
Verbs.example: Il a placé le livre sur la table.
Verbs.sourceExample: He placed the book on the table.

mistakes.fix: Il a placé le livre sur la table.
mistakes.sourceFix: He placed the book on the table.

Verbs.title: combinaisons de verbes
points: certains verbes sont suivis d'un infinitif avec to
utilisez to + base verb apr?s ces verbes
gardez l'infinitif juste apr?s le verbe principal
sourcePoints: one common verb combination is verb + to-infinitive
use to + base verb immediately after the main verb
do not omit to in this pattern

Verbs.title: verbes à particule
points: changement de sens avec des particules
sourcePoints: verb plus particle
separable phrasal verbs
meaning shift with particles

mistakes.wrong: Il a allumé et éteint la lumière.
mistakes.sourceWrong: He turned the light on off.

Tenses & Aspect.title: présent simple
sourcePoints: present simple for habits
present simple for facts
present simple for schedules

Tenses & Aspect.title: présent continu
points: présent continu pour les actions temporaires
présent continu pour les projets proches
sourcePoints: present continuous for now
present continuous for temporary actions
present continuous for near plans

Tenses & Aspect.title: passé simple
points: passé simple pour les actions terminées
passé simple pour les mots de temps passés
sourcePoints: past simple for finished actions
past simple for past time words
past simple for sequences
Tenses & Aspect.example: Ils ont visité Paris l'année dernière.

Tenses & Aspect.title: passé continu
sourcePoints: past continuous for background
past continuous with interruption
past continuous for two actions
Tenses & Aspect.example: Je cuisinais quand il a appelé.
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: I was cooking when he called.

mistakes.sourceWrong: She was cook when I called.
mistakes.sourceFix: She was cooking when I called.

Tenses & Aspect.title: passé composé
points: présent parfait pour les résultats récents
présent parfait avec depuis et pendant
sourcePoints: present perfect for experience
present perfect for recent results
present perfect with since and for
Tenses & Aspect.example: Il vit ici depuis des années.
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: He has lived here for years.

mistakes.sourceWrong: He has live here for years.
mistakes.sourceFix: He has lived here for years.

Tenses & Aspect.title: plus-que-parfait
points: plus-que-parfait pour cause dans le passé
sourcePoints: past perfect for earlier past
past perfect for cause in past
past perfect with before
Tenses & Aspect.example: Elle était partie avant que j'arrive.
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: She had left before I arrived.

mistakes.wrong: Il est parti quand je suis arrivé.
mistakes.fix: Il était parti quand je suis arrivé.
mistakes.sourceWrong: He had leave before I arrived.
mistakes.sourceFix: He had left before I arrived.

Tenses & Aspect.title: formes futures
sourcePoints: use will + base verb for one future form
use be going to + base verb for another future form
use present continuous + future time for arranged plans
Tenses & Aspect.example: Je t'appellerai ce soir. Je vais étudier plus tard. Je rencontre Sam demain.
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: I will call you tonight. I am going to study later. I am meeting Sam tomorrow.

mistakes.sourceWrong: She will going to call tomorrow.
mistakes.sourceFix: She is going to call tomorrow.

Tenses & Aspect.title: futur continu
points: futur continu pour une demande polie
sourcePoints: future continuous for progress
future continuous for background
future continuous for polite inquiry
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: I will be working at six.

mistakes.sourceFix: I will be working at six.

Tenses & Aspect.title: futur antérieur
sourcePoints: future perfect for deadlines
future perfect with by time
future perfect for completion
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: They will have finished by Friday.

mistakes.sourceWrong: They will have finish by Friday.
mistakes.sourceFix: They will have finished by Friday.

Tenses & Aspect.title: contrastes d'aspect
points: contraste de focalisation sur la durée
sourcePoints: simple vs continuous contrast
perfect vs simple contrast
duration focus contrast
Tenses & Aspect.example: Je travaille tous les jours, je travaille maintenant, et j'ai travaillé ici pendant des années.
Tenses & Aspect.sourceExample: I work every day. I am working now. I have worked here for years.

mistakes.sourceWrong: I have work here for years.
mistakes.sourceFix: I have worked here for years.

Nouns & Articles.title: noms dénombrables
points: un ou une avant les dénombrables
sourcePoints: countable nouns can be singular or plural
use a or an before singular countable nouns
use a number with plural countable nouns
Nouns & Articles.sourceExample: I have a coin and two apples.

mistakes.sourceWrong: I have coin and two apples.
mistakes.sourceFix: I have a coin and two apples.

Nouns & Articles.title: noms indénombrables
points: un morceau de pour les unités
sourcePoints: uncountable nouns usually do not have plural forms
use some with uncountable nouns
use a piece of for countable units
Nouns & Articles.sourceExample: We need some rice and a piece of bread.

mistakes.sourceFix: I need two pieces of bread.

Nouns & Articles.title: articles
points: un ou une pour la première mention
pas d'article pour des idées générales
sourcePoints: use a or an for first mention of a singular countable noun
use the when the noun is specific or already known
place the article directly before the noun
Nouns & Articles.sourceExample: I saw a dog. The dog is outside.

Nouns & Articles.title: formes plurielles
sourcePoints: use a plural noun for more than one
many plurals add -s or -es
some plurals are irregular (child -> children)
Nouns & Articles.sourceExample: Two apples and three children are here.

Nouns & Articles.title: noms possessifs
sourcePoints: add apostrophe + s to a singular noun to show ownership
place the possessive noun before the thing owned
keep the apostrophe in the correct position
Nouns & Articles.example: Le téléphone de Sara est nouveau.

mistakes.wrong: Le livre du professeur est nouveau.
mistakes.fix: Le livre du professeur est nouveau.

Nouns & Articles.title: groupes nominaux
sourcePoints: a noun phrase can include determiner + noun
an adjective can appear before the noun
keep the order determiner + adjective + noun
Nouns & Articles.example: La petite table de cuisine est cassée.

mistakes.wrong: Elle a acheté une robe rouge.
mistakes.fix: Elle a acheté une robe rouge.

Nouns & Articles.title: quantificateurs
sourcePoints: use many with plural countable nouns
use much with uncountable nouns
choose the quantifier by noun type
Nouns & Articles.sourceExample: There are many options, and there is much information.

Pronouns & Reference.title: pronoms sujets
sourcePoints: subject pronouns replace noun subjects (i, you, he, she, it, we, they)
use a subject pronoun before the main verb in statements
choose the pronoun that matches number and person

Pronouns & Reference.title: pronoms objets
points: position de l'objet après les verbes
sourcePoints: object pronouns replace noun objects (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
place object pronouns after the main verb
use object forms, not subject forms, in object position

Pronouns & Reference.title: formes possessives
points: le mien le tien pour autonome
sourcePoints: use possessive adjectives before nouns (my, your, his, her, our, their)
use possessive pronouns without a noun (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs)
do not add apostrophes to possessive pronouns
Pronouns & Reference.sourceExample: My bag is new. Hers is old.

Pronouns & Reference.title: pronoms réfléchis
sourcePoints: use reflexive pronouns when subject and object are the same
singular forms: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself
plural forms: ourselves, yourselves, themselves

Pronouns & Reference.title: démonstratifs
sourcePoints: use this and these for things near the speaker
use that and those for things farther away
use this or that with singular nouns and these or those with plural nouns

Pronouns & Reference.title: référence relative
sourcePoints: use who for people in relative clauses
use which for things in relative clauses
use that for people or things in defining relative clauses
Pronouns & Reference.example: L'homme qui a appelé est parti.
Pronouns & Reference.sourceExample: The man who called me left.

mistakes.sourceWrong: The man which called me left.
mistakes.sourceFix: The man who called me left.

Pronouns & Reference.title: référence indéfinie
sourcePoints: use someone and something in affirmative statements
use anyone and anything in negative statements and questions
use everyone and everything for complete groups

mistakes.sourceWrong: I saw anyone at the station.
mistakes.sourceFix: I saw someone at the station.

Modifiers.title: les bases des adjectifs
sourcePoints: adjectives describe nouns
adjectives can come before nouns
adjectives can come after linking verbs like be

Modifiers.title: l'ordre des adjectifs
sourcePoints: when several adjectives come before a noun, use a common order
opinion usually comes before size
size usually comes before color
Modifiers.example: Elle a acheté un petit sac rouge.
Modifiers.sourceExample: She bought a lovely small red bag.

mistakes.sourceWrong: She bought a red small bag.
mistakes.sourceFix: She bought a small red bag.

Modifiers.title: les comparatifs
sourcePoints: use comparatives to compare two things
many short adjectives take -er
many longer adjectives use more
Modifiers.example: Ceci est plus rapide que cela.

mistakes.sourceWrong: This is more faster than that.

Modifiers.title: les superlatifs
points: formes en est ou le plus
focus sur la comparaison de groupe
sourcePoints: use superlatives to compare one item with a group
many short adjectives take -est and longer adjectives use most
use the before superlative adjectives

Modifiers.title: les bases des adverbes
sourcePoints: adverbs can modify verbs
many adverbs of manner end in -ly
adverbs of manner usually come after the verb or object

Modifiers.title: les adverbes de fréquence
sourcePoints: common frequency adverbs include always, usually, often, sometimes, and never
place frequency adverbs before main verbs
place frequency adverbs after be

Modifiers.title: les adverbes de temps et de lieu
points: temps à la fin de la position
sourcePoints: place adverbs answer where and time adverbs answer when
in neutral order, place usually comes before time
both often appear near the end of the clause
Modifiers.example: Nous nous sommes rencontrés là-bas hier.

Modifiers.title: les mots de degré
sourcePoints: degree words modify adjectives or adverbs
use very to strengthen adjectives or adverbs
use enough after adjectives and adverbs

Modifiers.title: les participes
points: adjectifs en ing pour la cause
adjectifs en ed pour le sentiment
sourcePoints: use -ing adjectives for things that cause a feeling
use -ed adjectives for how people feel
do not mix -ing and -ed meanings
Modifiers.sourceExample: The movie was boring, and I was bored.

Modifiers.title: l'empilement des modificateurs
sourcePoints: when multiple modifiers appear, keep a clear order
put degree words before adjectives
keep manner adverbs in a natural position in the clause
Modifiers.example: Elle a rapidement répondu à la question difficile.
Modifiers.sourceExample: She answered the very difficult question quickly.

mistakes.wrong: Elle a acheté un nouveau petit sac rouge.
mistakes.fix: Elle a acheté un petit nouveau sac rouge.
mistakes.sourceWrong: She answered the difficult very question quickly.
mistakes.sourceFix: She answered the very difficult question quickly.

Questions.title: questions fermées
sourcePoints: use do, does, or did before the subject
use the base verb after the subject
end yes-no questions with a question mark

Questions.title: questions ouvertes
points: mot interrogatif + aux + sujet + verbe de base
sourcePoints: start with a wh word such as who, what, where, when, why, or how
place the auxiliary before the subject
use the base verb after the subject

Questions.title: questions avec être
sourcePoints: place be before the subject
do not use do or does with be questions
place the complement after the subject

Questions.title: questions avec faire
sourcePoints: use do, does, or did before the subject
keep the main verb in base form after do, does, or did
use did for past-time yes-no questions

Questions.title: questions avec des modaux
sourcePoints: place the modal before the subject
use the base verb after the subject
do not use do or does with modal questions

Questions.title: questions tag
sourcePoints: add a short tag after a statement
use a negative tag after a positive statement
use a positive tag after a negative statement

Questions.title: questions indirectes
sourcePoints: start with an introductory phrase such as could you tell me
use statement word order inside the embedded question
do not invert subject and verb inside the embedded question
Questions.sourceExample: Could you tell me where it is?

mistakes.fix: Peux-tu me dire où il est ?
mistakes.sourceWrong: Could you tell me where is it?
mistakes.sourceFix: Could you tell me where it is?

Negation.title: pas avec être
sourcePoints: use be + not to form negatives with be
place not after am, is, are, was, or were
keep the complement after the negative be form

Negation.title: pas avec faire
points: sujet + auxiliaire + ne + verbe à l'infinitif
sourcePoints: use do, does, or did + not to form negatives with main verbs
use does with he, she, and it in present simple
keep the main verb in base form after do, does, or did + not

Negation.title: formes courtes négatives
points: sujet + auxiliaire + ne + verbe à l'infinitif
sourcePoints: use short negative forms such as don't, doesn't, isn't, and aren't
keep the same word order as the full negative form
match the short form to the subject and auxiliary

Negation.title: mots négatifs
sourcePoints: common negative words include no, none, never, and nothing
use one negative form per clause in standard english
use any forms after not when needed (anyone, anything, anywhere)
Negation.example: Il n'y a pas de lait.

Negation.title: questions négatives
points: auxiliaire + ne + sujet + verbe à l'infinitif + objet
sourcePoints: form negative questions with auxiliary + n't + subject + base verb
use negative questions to check or confirm expectations
keep the main verb in base form after the auxiliary

Negation.title: négatifs limités
sourcePoints: limited negatives include hardly, barely, and rarely
in neutral statements, place them before the main verb
avoid adding a second negative in the same clause

Connections.title: connecteurs de base
sourcePoints: use and to add similar ideas
use but to show contrast
use or to show alternatives

mistakes.sourceFix: I called, but no one answered.

Connections.title: raison et résultat

sourcePoints: use because + clause to give a reason
use so + clause to show a result
keep both clauses complete

mistakes.sourceFix: I was late because the bus was late.

Connections.title: contraste et choix
sourcePoints: use but or although to show contrast
use either ... or ... to show a choice
use one connector pattern at a time
Connections.example: Elle est partie, bien qu'elle fût fatiguée.

Connections.title: connecteurs temporels
sourcePoints: use when for events at the same time
use before and after to order events
keep tense forms natural in time clauses

Connections.title: liens de comparaison
sourcePoints: use like before a noun phrase
use as for role or function
use than after comparative forms

mistakes.fix: Elle est plus grande que moi.

Connections.title: ajout d'idées
sourcePoints: use also to add one more idea
use in addition for a more formal add-on
place the addition marker in a clear position
Connections.example: Nous avons aussi besoin de chaises.

Connections.title: ordonnancement des idées
sourcePoints: use first, then, and finally to show sequence
keep events in chronological order
use one clear sequence marker per step
Connections.example: D'abord nous planifions, ensuite nous agissons.
Connections.sourceExample: First we plan, then we act.

mistakes.sourceFix: First we met, then we left.

Conditions.title: conditions réelles
sourcePoints: use if + present simple for real and possible conditions

mistakes.fix: Si tu viens, nous nous rencontrons.

mistakes.sourceFix: If you press this, it starts.

Conditions.title: conditions futures
sourcePoints: use if + present simple for future conditions
use will + base verb in the result clause
do not use will in the if clause

mistakes.sourceWrong: If it will be sunny, we will go.
mistakes.sourceFix: If it is sunny, we will go.

Conditions.title: présent irréel
sourcePoints: use if + past simple for unreal present situations
use would + base verb in the result clause

mistakes.sourceFix: If I had time, I would go.

sourcePoints: use if + past perfect for unreal past situations

mistakes.fix: Si j'avais su, je l'aurais dit.
mistakes.sourceWrong: If I knew, I would have told.
mistakes.sourceFix: If I had known, I would have told.

Conditions.title: conditions mixtes
points: si clause (plus-que-parfait) + résultat présent (conditionnel + verbe à l'infinitif)
sourcePoints: use if + past perfect for a past condition
use would + base verb for a present result
mixed conditionals connect past causes to present consequences
Conditions.example: Si elle avait étudié, elle serait calme maintenant.
Conditions.sourceExample: If she had studied, she would be calm now.

mistakes.wrong: Si j'étudiais, j'aurais le poste maintenant.
mistakes.fix: Si j'avais étudié, j'aurais le poste maintenant.
mistakes.sourceWrong: If I studied harder, I would have the job now.
mistakes.sourceFix: If I had studied harder, I would have the job now.

Conditions.title: sauf et autrement
sourcePoints: use unless to mean if ... not
use present simple after unless for future meaning
keep result and condition clauses clear and complete
Conditions.example: Nous irons à moins qu'il ne pleuve.
Conditions.sourceExample: We will go unless it rains.

mistakes.wrong: Nous irons à moins qu'il ne pleuve.
mistakes.fix: Nous irons à moins qu'il ne pleuve.
mistakes.sourceWrong: We will go unless it will rain.
mistakes.sourceFix: We will go unless it rains.

Voice & Focus.title: voix active
sourcePoints: in active voice, the doer is the subject
use subject + action verb + object order
active voice usually sounds more direct and clear
Voice & Focus.example: Le chef a préparé le dîner.

mistakes.wrong: Le gâteau a été cuit par ma mère.
mistakes.fix: Ma mère a cuit le gâteau.
mistakes.sourceWrong: Dinner was cooked by the chef.

Voice & Focus.title: voix passive
sourcePoints: in passive voice, the receiver becomes the subject
use be + past participle in the verb phrase
add by + doer only when the doer is important

mistakes.fix: Le rapport a été terminé hier.

mistakes.sourceFix: The meal was cooked by the chef.

Voice & Focus.title: changement de focus

separate the fronted phrase with a comma
keep the rest of the clause in normal order
Voice & Focus.example: Ce livre, je l'ai fini hier.

mistakes.fix: Ce livre, je l'ai acheté hier.

Voice & Focus.title: phrases éclatées
points: sujet il + phrase de focus + proposition
sourcePoints: use it + be to highlight one part of the sentence
follow the focus with who or that + clause
use who for people and that for things

Voice & Focus.title: sujets 'il' et 'il y a'
points: sujet il y a + verbe être + nom
sourcePoints: use there + be to introduce new information
use it + be for weather, time, and distance
match the be verb with the real noun phrase

mistakes.fix: Il y a un problème dans la pièce.
mistakes.sourceWrong: There are a problem in the room.
mistakes.sourceFix: There is a problem in the room.

Modality.title: capacité
sourcePoints: use can and could to express ability
place the modal before the base verb
do not add to after can or could

Modality.title: permission
sourcePoints: use can, may, or could to ask for permission
in questions, place the modal before the subject
use the base verb after the modal without to

Modality.title: obligation
sourcePoints: use must for strong obligation
use have to for external obligation
after must, use the base verb without to
Modality.example: Vous devez porter une ceinture de sécurité.

mistakes.sourceWrong: You must to wear a badge.

Modality.title: conseil
sourcePoints: use should or ought to to give advice
use should + base verb
use ought to + base verb

Modality.title: possibilité
sourcePoints: use may or might to express possibility
place the modal before the base verb
do not add to after may or might

Modality.title: probabilité
points: sujet + modal + mot de probabilité + verbe à l'infinitif
sourcePoints: use will + probably + base verb for likely future events
place probably after will in this pattern
keep the main verb in base form after the probability marker

Modality.title: demandes polies
points: modal + sujet + verbe à l'infinitif + objet
sourcePoints: use could or would for polite requests
use modal + subject + base verb + object order
you can add please for extra politeness

mistakes.fix: Pourriez-vous ouvrir la porte, s'il vous plaît ?

Modality.title: offres et invitations
sourcePoints: use would you like + noun for offers
use would you like to + base verb for invitations
do not use do you like for formal offers or invitations

Reported Speech.title: rapport des déclarations
sourcePoints: report statements with said (that) + clause
that is optional in many neutral sentences
adjust pronouns and time words as needed
Reported Speech.example: Elle a dit qu'elle était prête.

mistakes.fix: Elle a dit qu'elle était fatiguée.
mistakes.sourceWrong: She said me she was tired.

Reported Speech.title: rapport des questions
sourcePoints: use asked if or whether for yes-no questions
use asked + wh-word for information questions
use statement word order in the reported clause
Reported Speech.example: Il a demandé si j'allais bien.
Reported Speech.sourceExample: He asked if I was okay.

mistakes.wrong: Il a demandé où est la gare.
mistakes.fix: Il a demandé où était la gare.
mistakes.sourceWrong: He asked where is the station.
mistakes.sourceFix: He asked where the station was.

Reported Speech.title: rapport des demandes
sourcePoints: report requests with asked + object + to + base verb
keep the infinitive form after to
keep the request meaning without direct question form

mistakes.wrong: Elle m'a demandé si je peux aider.

Reported Speech.title: rapport des ordres
sourcePoints: report commands with told or ordered + object + to + base verb
keep the base verb after to
preserve command meaning in indirect form
Reported Speech.example: Il nous a dit de partir.

Reported Speech.title: les bases du décalage
sourcePoints: backshift present to past in many past reporting contexts
backshift will to would
backshift can to could when needed
Reported Speech.example: Ils ont dit qu'ils avaient le temps.

mistakes.wrong: Elle a dit qu'elle est prête.
mistakes.fix: Elle a dit qu'elle était prête.

Reported Speech.title: changements de temps et de lieu
sourcePoints: change now to then when context requires
change here to there when reference point shifts
change today to that day in past reporting contexts
Reported Speech.example: Il a dit qu'il était là.

mistakes.wrong: Il a dit qu'il viendra ici aujourd'hui.
mistakes.fix: Il a dit qu'il viendrait là-bas ce jour-là.
mistakes.sourceWrong: He said he would come here today.
mistakes.sourceFix: He said he would come there that day.

Formality & Style.title: formel vs informel
sourcePoints: use formal wording in professional or unfamiliar contexts
use informal wording with friends and familiar contexts
keep register consistent within the same sentence

mistakes.sourceWrong: In a formal email, Hey, could you assist me?
mistakes.sourceFix: In a formal email, Could you assist me?

Formality & Style.title: contractions
sourcePoints: contractions are common in casual speech and writing
use apostrophes correctly in contractions
choose full forms in very formal writing when needed
Formality & Style.example: Je ne peux pas rester longtemps.

mistakes.wrong: Je suis en retard, ne m'attendez pas.
mistakes.fix: Je suis en retard, ne m'attendez pas.

Formality & Style.title: adoucir poliment
points: s'il vous plaît pour la politesse
sourcePoints: use could or would to soften requests
add please when extra politeness is needed
avoid bare imperatives in formal requests

Formality & Style.title: oral vs écrit
points: contrôle de la longueur des phrases
sourcePoints: spoken language allows informal markers and shortcuts
written language prefers clear complete sentences
avoid slang in formal written contexts

mistakes.wrong: Dans un écrit formel : Je suis arrivé(e) lol.
mistakes.fix: Dans un écrit formel : Je suis arrivé.
mistakes.sourceWrong: In formal writing, I arrived lol.

Formality & Style.title: style professionnel
sourcePoints: state your purpose clearly and politely
keep a neutral and respectful tone
use a polite closing when appropriate

mistakes.wrong: Salut, j'ai besoin de ça dès que possible.
mistakes.fix: Bonjour, j'ai besoin de cela rapidement.

Formality & Style.title: style décontracté
sourcePoints: casual style uses friendly greetings
short and simple wording is common
avoid overly formal openings in casual contexts

mistakes.wrong: Monsieur ou Madame, comment ça va ?
mistakes.sourceWrong: Dear Sam, how is it going?

Formality & Style.title: clarté et concision
sourcePoints: use short direct sentences
remove unnecessary filler words
put the main point early
Formality & Style.example: Nous avons besoin d'une réponse rapide.

mistakes.wrong: Étant donné qu'il pleut, nous n'irons pas.
mistakes.fix: Il pleut, donc nous n'irons pas.
mistakes.sourceWrong: We need a quick answer at this point in time.

Discourse & Flow.title: ouverture et fermeture
sourcePoints: open with a greeting at the start
end with a clear closing signal
keep opening and closing matched to the context
Discourse & Flow.example: Salut tout le monde, de toute façon, c'est tout pour aujourd'hui.
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: Hi everyone, that is all for today.

mistakes.fix: Salut, je voulais parler. Merci, au revoir.
mistakes.sourceWrong: Anyway, that is all for today.
mistakes.sourceFix: Hi everyone, that is all for today.

Discourse & Flow.title: changements de sujet
sourcePoints: use a shift marker like by the way to change topic
add a complete clause after the shift marker
avoid abrupt topic jumps without a marker
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: By the way, I have news.

mistakes.wrong: Au fait, à cause du planning.
mistakes.fix: Au fait, pouvons-nous parler du planning ?
mistakes.sourceWrong: By the way, about the schedule.
mistakes.sourceFix: By the way, can we talk about the schedule?

Discourse & Flow.title: outils de cohésion
sourcePoints: use reference words like it or this to connect ideas
use a linker to show the relation between clauses
make each reference clear and easy to track
Discourse & Flow.example: Cette idée se connecte au dernier point.
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: I bought a book, and it is useful.

mistakes.wrong: J'ai acheté un livre. Le livre est nouveau.
mistakes.fix: J'ai acheté un livre. Il est nouveau.
mistakes.sourceWrong: I bought a book, and book is useful.
mistakes.sourceFix: I bought a book, and it is useful.

Discourse & Flow.title: séquençage des idées
sourcePoints: use sequence markers like first and then
keep event order clear for the listener or reader
do not repeat the same sequence marker
Discourse & Flow.example: D'abord nous faisons nos bagages, puis nous partons.
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: First we pack, then we leave.

mistakes.wrong: D'abord, je suis parti, puis je me suis réveillé.
mistakes.fix: D'abord, je me suis réveillé, puis je suis parti.
mistakes.sourceWrong: First we pack, first we leave.
mistakes.sourceFix: First we pack, then we leave.

Discourse & Flow.title: mouvements de clarification
sourcePoints: use a clarification phrase to check meaning
ask a direct clarification question when needed
name the exact item you want to clarify
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: Do you mean the morning meeting?

mistakes.sourceFix: Do you mean the morning meeting?

Discourse & Flow.title: résumés
sourcePoints: use a summary marker like in short or to sum up
state only the main point in the summary line
keep summary sentences short and direct

mistakes.fix: En résumé, nous avons besoin de plus de temps.
mistakes.sourceFix: In short, we need more time.

Discourse & Flow.title: emphase et répétition
sourcePoints: use do or really to add emphasis when needed
place emphasis words in natural positions
avoid unnecessary repeated words
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: I do need your answer today.

mistakes.wrong: Je ne veux pas y aller.
mistakes.sourceWrong: I need really your answer today.
mistakes.sourceFix: I really need your answer today.

Discourse & Flow.title: flux de conversation
sourcePoints: use listening signals to show attention
use turn-taking signals to guide the next speaker
keep transitions polite and clear
Discourse & Flow.example: Je vois, s'il vous plaît continuez.

mistakes.wrong: Moi aussi. Et toi, tu es ?

Discourse & Flow.title: donner des exemples
sourcePoints: use markers like for example or for instance
follow the marker with a complete example clause
keep the example directly related to your point
Discourse & Flow.example: Par exemple, appelez le service d'assistance.
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: For example, call the help desk.

mistakes.fix: Par exemple, c'est utile pour voyager.
mistakes.sourceFix: For example, call the help desk.

Discourse & Flow.title: réparation et correction
sourcePoints: use repair markers like sorry or I mean
state the correction immediately after the marker
replace only the incorrect part
Discourse & Flow.sourceExample: Sorry, I mean Tuesday, not Monday.

mistakes.fix: Désolé, je veux dire que je pars.
